headline: In 1933 the US made it illegal for citizens to own more than a handful of gold coins

sources.title: Executive Order 6102 — full text (The American Presidency Project, UC Santa Barbara)
Federal Reserve History — Gold Reserve Act

summary: On 5 April 1933, President Franklin D. Roosevelt signed Executive Order 6102, requiring everyone in the continental United States to hand over gold coin, gold bullion and gold certificates to the Federal Reserve by 1 May 1933, in exchange for a fixed $20.67 per troy ounce. People could keep only up to $100 worth (about 5 ounces) plus coins of recognized collector value. Violators faced a fine of up to $10,000, up to 10 years in prison, or both. The order was issued under the WWI-era Trading with the Enemy Act (as amended by the 1933 Emergency Banking Act) — a war-powers law turned against ordinary Americans' own savings. Less than a year later, the Gold Reserve Act of 1934 revalued gold to $35/oz, letting the government profit from gold it had just compelled citizens to sell at the lower price. The order was repealed effective 31 December 1974 (Public Law 93-373). In 2026 dollars (US CPI, ~25.6×), $20.67/oz is about $530 and the $100 exemption about $2,600 — far below today's actual gold price, because gold itself has outpaced general inflation since 1933.
